The ASGI adapter: read the request, hand it to the pipeline, write the reply.

Deliberately thin. All the security is in `dispatch_request` - headers, CORS,
rate limit, authentication, step-up, permission - so that swapping the server
cannot accidentally swap out a gate. This layer parses bytes and nothing else.

It also serves the workspace. Static files are read from one directory with a
containment check; there is no endpoint anywhere that takes a path.

The order is computed from the foreign keys that exist right now, not
written down here. Forty-four tables carry org_id and most have no key
back to organisation, so a hand-kept list would be one migration away
from leaving a customer's alerts on disk with nothing pointing at them.

Tables are sorted so that anything referencing another table is emptied
before the table it references. A cycle - none exist today - falls back to
the order it was found in, and the delete would fail loudly rather than
half-finish quietly.

there is nothing in this path that would substitute anything into it.

A run is recorded whether or not it found something. "This hunt has run
every week for a year and never hit" is a finding about the query, and a
platform that only stores hits cannot tell you that.

exports.doc:

collections by uuid and nobody can configure a feed against a uuid they have

selected outright - that is the common case, and making someone pick from a
list of one is ceremony.
exports.name: execute_taxii_discovery

exports.doc:
Poll one TAXII collection, incrementally, page by page.

The watermark is the whole point. Each poll asks for what the server accepted
since the last one, and the watermark advances ONLY after the indicators are
committed - move it first and a failed write skips everything that page
carried, with nothing anywhere to say so.

Both paging schemes are handled: 2.1 follows the envelope cursor, 2.0 walks
the Range header and treats 416 as the end of the collection rather than a
failure. A cursor that does not advance ends the loop, because a server that
keeps answering `more: true` with the same page would otherwise be an
infinite poll.
exports.name: execute_taxii_poll

exports.doc:
Poll one TAXII collection, incrementally, page by page.

The watermark is the whole point. Each poll asks for what the server accepted
since the last one, and the watermark advances ONLY after the indicators are
committed - move it first and a failed write skips everything that page
carried, with nothing anywhere to say so.

Both paging schemes are handled: 2.1 follows the envelope cursor, 2.0 walks
the Range header and treats 416 as the end of the collection rather than a
failure. A cursor that does not advance ends the loop, because a server that
keeps answering `more: true` with the same page would otherwise be an
infinite poll.

The installation seeds no user, so this is the only way in. It runs from a
shell on the deployment rather than over HTTP, which is the point: the
authority to create the first administrator is the authority to run commands

with no permissions at all - so an account without a factor cannot finish
signing in. And the role grant refuses to attach admin.* to an account with
no factor, so doing it later would mean doing it in the wrong order.

Read this before writing a containment playbook. EDR response actions are NOT
interchangeable: CrowdStrike contains at the agent and keeps its own cloud
reachable; Defender offers a Selective mode that leaves Teams and Outlook
working; SentinelOne disconnects the interface outright; Cybereason has no
app-restriction concept at all. A playbook that assumes they are the same
produces a containment that is either weaker or far more disruptive than the
analyst intended, and finds that out during the incident.

`unsupported` carries as much weight as `supported`. A platform that silently
skips an action it cannot perform has told the analyst the host is contained
when it is not, which is the single worst lie a SOAR can tell.

exports.doc:
Where the next poll should resume from.

The server's own X-TAXII-Date-Added-Last is preferred, because it refers to
when the server accepted the object, which is what `added_after` filters on.
An object's `modified` is a different clock and using it as a substitute is
the classic way to miss objects that were added late but modified early.

When the header is absent the newest `modified` is the only thing available,
and it is imprecise enough that the next poll may re-read a few objects.
That is the safe direction: ingestion is an upsert, so re-reading costs
nothing, while skipping loses indicators silently.

A watermark never moves backwards.
exports.name: advance_watermark

`added_after` is the point of the whole exercise: ask only for what arrived
since the last poll. Without it every poll re-reads the entire collection,
which is slow, gets the client rate-limited, and looks exactly like a feed
that is stuck.

TAXII 2.0 has no limit or next parameter - it pages with the Range header -
so it gets only the filter.

getting it wrong looks like an auth or a routing problem and is neither.
The objects endpoint is the odd one: in 2.0 it returns STIX and carries the
STIX media type, while in 2.1 it returns a TAXII envelope.

a watermark backwards and silently re-read a collection every poll.

real servers return paths - the ATT&CK TAXII server answers `/api/v21/` -
so taking them literally produces a request with no scheme and a confusing

that is stuck.

so it gets only the filter.
exports.name: taxii_page_query

exports.doc:
Where the next poll should resume from.

The server's own X-TAXII-Date-Added-Last is preferred, because it refers to
when the server accepted the object, which is what `added_after` filters on.
An object's `modified` is a different clock and using it as a substitute is
the classic way to miss objects that were added late but modified early.

When the header is absent the newest `modified` is the only thing available,
and it is imprecise enough that the next poll may re-read a few objects.
That is the safe direction: ingestion is an upsert, so re-reading costs
nothing, while skipping loses indicators silently.
